result:
The trees outside my window are bare, their branches like dark veins against a bruised-grey sky. It’s a stark sight, but not an ugly one. There is a certain, quiet honesty to a world stripped of pretense. The greenery is gone, the lushness is a memory, and all that remains is the essential structure—the raw, reaching framework of the thing itself.

I think we spend a lot of our lives wrapped in our own foliage, busy with the leaves of daily tasks and transient emotions. We forget about the bones of who we are. An afternoon like this, one that settles into the house with a heavy, still presence, asks for a different kind of attention. It asks you to pause and look past the surface.

There is a rhythm here, too. In the starkness of the trees, one can almost see the slow, sure flow of sap drawing inward, conserving its strength for the long wait. It’s a lesson in patience. The tree doesn't struggle against the winter; it simply recalibrates. It trusts the process.

And so, I sit here, following its lead. Letting the chatter of my own mind fall away like so many autumn leaves, and finding a strange, fragile peace in simply being the shape that is left.
